extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, mineralogists, botanists and informed scientific readers (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, methods and evaluative comments for 19th-century natural-history research, museum curation, and journal reporting (mineralogy, botany, ethnology, paleontology, surveying). Includes experimental controls, analytical techniques, and expectations for scientific publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize hydrography and orography in ethnological origin studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of studying the hydrography and orography of a country before attempting to trace the origin of its inhabitants: "Mountains and streams afford more stable evidence in regard to ethnological centres of origin than the ever-fluctuating combinations of language."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use physical geography (mountains, rivers) as primary, stable evidence when reconstructing migration and origin hypotheses; treat linguistic evidence as more variable and less determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly civility in ethnological journals
rubrics_metrics.description: An ethnological journal is not the place for international warfare; avoid allowing personal rancour and national hate to overweigh scholarly argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain courteous, reasoned tone in academic publications; do not let personal or national animosities substitute for evidence-based argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and substantive contribution for journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to a specialist journal should offer more than a résumé of semi-popular works: criticism of Dr. Martens’ paper as "little more than a résumé of what G. E. Rumph, P. Bonanni, Johnson, and Mr. Woodward have given."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal submissions should present new analysis, data, or interpretation rather than summarising existing popular treatments; editors/readers expect original scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical separation methods for meteorite/component analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating the whole meteoritic mass with mercuric chloride at 100° dissolves the iron and troilite, leaving an unattacked crystalline 'magma' that can be fractionated into constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted chemical reagents under controlled conditions to remove metallic phases and isolate silicate/other components prior to mineral identification; record reagent, temperature, and duration (e.g., mercuric chloride at 100° for several hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral identification by combined physical and chemical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify minerals using specific gravity, hardness, colour changes upon acid treatment, crystal habit, and quantitative analyses (e.g., hydrogen-fluoride distillation and fusion with mixed alkaline carbonates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a suite of diagnostic tests (density, hardness, reaction to acids, microscopic habit) and corroborate with chemical analyses; compare results with literature values and known specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical mineralogy tests for optic sign and dispersion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use convergent polarized light, quarter-undulation plates before and after the crystal, analyzer rotation, and observation of coloured rings/brushes to determine optic character (positive/negative) and dispersion effects in uniaxial and biaxial crystals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ combinations of polariser/analyser, quarter-wave plates, and controlled rotation to observe ring behaviour (contraction/expansion, presence/absence of brushes), centre brightness/darkness changes, and dispersion; use these observations as diagnostic tests of optic sign and dispersion produced by plates or the crystal itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for marine soundings and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundings for planned submarine telegraph lines 'should be accompanied by dredgings, and ... carefully made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surveying submarine routes, perform dredging in conjunction with depth soundings to sample seabed composition and verify bathymetric measurements; ensure thorough, carefully conducted surveys especially in geologically interesting areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental controls and protocols for Drosera sensitivity studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls used to show that Drosera-hair contraction is not due to heat or perspiration: animal substances cooled before placement still act; property transmitted across fine waxed paper; substances coated with wax still effective; repeated moistening/drying used to prepare samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with controls to exclude alternative explanations (thermal, chemical contamination, perspiration). Use barriers (waxed paper, wax coatings) and temperature controls, prepare samples consistently (e.g., moistening/drying cycles), and report timing of responses (e.g., contraction often begins ~15 minutes, may complete after several hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of reversibility as validation in physiological experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants rendered insensitive by contact with albumen were restored to normal responsiveness after twenty-four hours placed on packets of sulphate of quinine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reversible manipulation (removal/antagonist treatment) where possible to strengthen causality claims; demonstrate that the effect can be reversed or the system restored as evidence the change was due to the experimental treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopy and polarized-light criteria for diatom structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of polarized light can show the siliceous investment of diatoms polarises light and contains iron-oxide; frustules may be composed of numerous minute individualised cells, with papillae causing moniliform markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply polarized-light microscopy to detect silica's optical behaviour and associated iron-oxide compounds; examine fine structure at high magnification to resolve cell units and papillae that produce surface ornamentation; avoid assuming frustules are single-celled without detailed observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum curation and preservation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Preservation of restorations and public-spirited conservation is praised; destruction of scientific restorations (e.g., Hawkins’ Central Park restorations) is condemned, contrasted with the preservation of the megalithic monument at Avebury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Museums and custodians should preserve scientific restorations and artefacts; destructive actions that impair scientific value are subject to public and professional reprobation; decisions affecting collections should consider scientific and cultural preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for taxonomic/paleontological descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When new species are described (e.g., Prof. Marsh's new Hadrosaurus and pterosaur remains), full measurements and locality information are provided and specimens deposited in institutions (e.g., Academy of Sciences of Philadelphia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete morphological measurements, clear diagnoses, precise locality data, and specimen deposition information when describing new taxa to allow verification and comparison; include illustrations/plates where helpful.
